name: Clinical systems
description: The records and messaging systems of a care organization: EHR screens in normal, degraded and read-only states, downtime reports and paper forms, interface status and HL7 and FHIR message views, results backlogs and reconciliation worklists. Used by health informatics, healthcare, nursing and pharmacy exercises. Every patient is synthetic.
outsideParties: the laboratory, radiology and pharmacy system vendors
the state immunization and lab reporting systems

advisorRoles.name: Clinical informatics liaison
advisorRoles.description: Explains what the EHR, the downtime tools and the interfaces can and cannot do, and which workflows have a paper fallback.

advisorRoles.name: Interface analyst liaison
advisorRoles.description: Reads the interface queues and says what replaying, holding or discarding a message class would do to orders and results.

advisorRoles.name: Health information management liaison
advisorRoles.description: Speaks for the legal record: what paper must be kept, how back-entry is indexed and what a merge or unmerge does to the record.

metrics.label: Declaration to all units on downtime procedures
Orders and results lost, delayed or duplicated
Restore order against the clinician priority list

decisionForms.label: Declare downtime
decisionForms.description: Declare planned or unplanned downtime of one or more clinical systems and say who is told.

decisionForms.label: Set restore order
decisionForms.description: Rank the systems and interfaces in the order they come back, with the reason for the sequence.

fields.label: Systems and interfaces, first to last (for example: identity check, lab interface, EHR, pharmacy interface)

decisionForms.label: Hold, replay or discard a message class
decisionForms.description: Decide what happens to the queued messages of one class (for example results from the laboratory feed).

decisionForms.label: Release or hold results
decisionForms.description: Release queued results to the chart now, or hold them until they are validated.

decisionForms.label: Open a duplicate or overlay merge
decisionForms.description: Start a merge or unmerge for two patient records, or freeze them.

decisionForms.label: Isolate devices
decisionForms.description: Take a class of networked devices off the network and name the manual alternative.

decisionForms.label: Notify
decisionForms.description: Tell a person, team or outside party what has happened.

decisionForms.label: Return to normal
decisionForms.description: End downtime procedures for one or more systems and say what is still open.

decisionForms.label: Report reconciliation progress
decisionForms.description: After recovery, record how far one unit has got with entering its paper records and how many discrepancies it found.

decisionForms.label: Close reconciliation
decisionForms.description: End the reconciliation and say what is still open.

glossary.definition: A planned or unplanned period when a clinical system is unavailable; care continues on paper procedures.
A copy of recent chart data that cannot be changed; it shows when its data is current as of.
A printed census, medication or results list; only as current as its as-of time.
Entering paper records into the system after recovery.
Comparing paper, system and department records to find missing, duplicated or misfiled orders and results.
Software routing HL7 v2 and FHIR messages between the EHR, lab, radiology, pharmacy and devices, with queues and an error queue.
HL7 v2 message families: admit/discharge/transfer, order, observation result.
Two patients sharing one record; more dangerous than a duplicate (one patient, two records).
Medical record number, assigned by the facility.

productConventions: Every downtime report states its as-of time and the printing system.
A read-only viewer shows a data-age stamp such as "Data current as of 14:05".
Paper forms carry a patient label area, a form version and a line saying they are entered after recovery.
Critical results are phoned with read-back and logged, never only emailed.
HL7 v2 uses pipe-delimited segments (MSH, PID, PV1, ORC, OBR, OBX); the decoded view must match the raw text.
Status colors always carry words: green OK, amber degraded, red down.
Mark exercise products as exercises; all patients and record numbers are fictional.
realismRules: Past incidents are history: cite them dated and attributed, never as current events.
Never use a real person's data; follow the record number format in the scenario facts.
A downtime report cannot show anything newer than its as-of time.
An interface queue grows at arrival rate minus drain rate.
Interfaces restart in order: registration (ADT) first so later orders and results find their patient, then orders and results; queues are emptied or held before an interface is stopped or restarted.

Opening the EHR to clinicians before the results interfaces have caught up leaves a chart that looks complete but is missing results; releasing results before downtime registrations are matched to the master patient index risks wrong-patient results.
Downtime registration uses a reserved record number block; duplicates after recovery are expected.
Clinical content is plausible exercise content, not a clinical reference; no dosing or treatment advice.
The hospital's compliance office decides what satisfies a requirement; say "may support".
Name no real hospital, health system or EHR product.
